title: The Loudest Animal on Earth Clicks at 230 Decibels

scenes.text: The loudest animal on Earth clicks at 230 decibels.
The sperm whale. One click, louder than any other animal sound ever measured.
A third of its body is head, and most of that head is a giant case of oil that focuses the sound.
It fires the clicks into the dark to find squid a thousand metres down. Then clicks faster and faster as it closes in.
It holds its breath up to 90 minutes down there.
230 decibels. Then it eats the squid.

description:
Sperm whale echolocation clicks have been measured at up to 230 decibels, the loudest sound made by any animal.
About a third of the whale's body is its head, which holds the spermaceti organ, a huge oil-filled case that focuses the clicks. The whale uses them to hunt squid as deep as 1,000 metres, speeding up the clicks as it closes in, and can stay down for up to 90 minutes.
What's the loudest animal you've heard in real life? Comment below.
first_comment: Divers who've been near clicking sperm whales describe feeling the clicks in their chest like a drum. Would you get in the water with one?
